scope: All 29 assigned candidates; no product edits, native or network runtime, deployments, or operator data accessed.

Both quarantine files have constant names and fs::write replaces existing contents; neither existence rejection nor a per-run directory preserves prior bundles. A second quarantine in the same writable working directory overwrites the first. This is source-level evidence of retention failure, not an executed loss of operator data.

candidates.rationale: The nonzero-remainder BA.EXACT path multiplies by 60 only once and divides with integer truncation. For value 1 and divisor 7 it stores 8 at scale 1, representing 8/60 rather than 1/7, and appends BA.EXACT without testing the new remainder. Current source still contains the candidate defect.

candidates.rationale: generate_hardware_pcr_quote computes two ordinary SHA-256 digests and emits tpm_quote_signature plus TPM_2_0_HARDWARE_SEALED. Its default seed is the hardware UUID returned in the same object. Reading a UUID, or using an environment seed, does not invoke TPM/Secure Enclave signing. The misleading object is attached to certificate/decision evidence and AL3 session data. No hardware identity or real secret was read during this review.

candidates.rationale: Linux ELF metadata has an empty section list, which prevents the Capstone section reader from yielding instructions. The fallback selects objdump -d, then rejects every nonempty colon-bearing line unless it begins 0x. Ordinary ADDRESS: instruction records consequently disappear before address parsing. This supports empty Linux disassembly for ordinary objdump output; no native disassembler was launched.

source_checks.observation: ELF sections are empty and empty Capstone output triggers CLI fallback.
No matching section returns an empty instruction list.
The objdump branch and colon filter discard normal address records.

guards: CLI errors also return an empty list, which does not distinguish parse failure from no instructions.
Mach-O/otool formatting is outside this finding.

candidates.rationale: Both instruction classifiers use finite mnemonic lists that omit x86 jle/jge/ja/jae/jb/jbe and ARM b.ge/b.le/b.hi/b.ls. Capstone output with one of these mnemonics gets is_branch=False and no branch target, so build_cfg does not make the required leaders or taken edge. The defect is independent of the Linux objdump parsing failure and remains reachable for Capstone disassembly with available sections.

source_checks.observation: Capstone branch list and target extraction omit the listed conditional mnemonics.
CLI branch list has the same omissions.
Leaders depend on branch/call/return flags.
Taken and fallthrough branch edges depend on is_branch.

guards: Listed mnemonics receive branch handling; call and return flags cover only their separate classes.
No decoder or CFG runtime was invoked.

candidates.rationale: The router adds the completion and WebSocket handlers without auth middleware. Completion extracts only state/JSON; WebSocket drops state and acknowledges channel/RPC messages without credentials. DualPasskeyAuth is instantiated but targeted source search finds no validate call. Main binds both HTTP listeners to loopback, so the confirmed exposure is to clients able to reach local ports; remote network access or actual privileged effects via RPC are not established.

guards: Loopback binding narrows reachability; it does not authenticate local clients.

candidates.rationale: The SCITT receipt digest hashes only invariant IDs, omitting each outcome, description and detail. Flipping outcomes for the same IDs changes claims but leaves the digest and fabricated sig_ed25519_ prefix unchanged. No signing key or Ed25519 operation is used, and Article 15 compliance is literal True. This is separate from the checks returning constants: even caller-supplied failing outcomes produce an unbound, unsigned receipt.

source_checks.observation: Receipt hashes IDs only, emits literal compliance and formats a pseudo-signature.
Both SCITT and JSON modes expose the pseudo-receipt.

guards: Process exit status may signal failed invariants, but the receipt compliance field and pseudo-signature remain unaffected.
No claim that an independent cryptographic verifier accepts the string.

candidates.rationale: IpcEnvelope publicly exposes independent len and fixed data[8192]. subscribe_exergy_packet slices data[..env.len] before unpack can reject malformed data, so len >8192 causes a bounds panic. The helper publisher bounds its own packets, but that does not constrain other publishers of the same service type. Current hypervisor writer also repeats the unchecked slice, extending the static scope beyond the unused convenience subscriber. No IPC publisher/subscriber runtime was executed.

source_checks.observation: Public envelope has no length invariant encoded in its type.
Helper publisher checks only its own packed payload.
Receive path slices untrusted len without a prior bound check.
Writer daemon uses IpcEnvelope and repeats unchecked slicing before unpack.

guards: Service connection/type compatibility and access to the IPC service are prerequisites.
ExergyPacket::unpack validation runs after slicing and cannot catch the bounds panic.
Worker stop flag and max_events bound looping, not envelope length.
